# QualifiedCalculator

Figma: [08s. QualifiedCalculator](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=3658-126638) · Family: 08 Safqah-Specific · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-01-01

A numeric-keypad calculator for qualified investors - enter an amount, see the projected return (APR · duration · net payout). Amount presets 10K/300K/400K/2M plus a Wallet top-up/withdraw mode. RTL.

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/qualified-calculator/reference.png`

### QualifiedCalculator Header

Result header above the keypad: projected total with +% delta, net profit, duration and annual rate line, and the typed investment amount; wallet types show balance and annual top-up cap.

Level: molecule · Contains: ProgressBar, Button · Part of: QualifiedCalculator

Use when:
- Top of QualifiedCalculator
- Type=wallet for wallet top-up/withdraw

Don't use when:
- Never alone without an input; use QualifiedCalculator

Accessibility: Announce updated projection while typing (polite).

Compliance: Figures are projections: label them expected (متوقع), show net after the agency fee (1% of profit, never of capital) beside gross, and never imply a guaranteed return.

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

A focused, full-screen calculator: the result header shows the projected return for the typed amount, and the on-screen keypad drives input. Qualified investors get higher caps and the Wallet mode.

Note: previews on this page are PNG exports - the component nests the remote Headling library component, whose Arabic is still IBM Plex Sans Arabic (unloadable here), so live instances aren’t possible until it’s re-fonted in its library.

### Anatomy

Two parts: the result Header (typed amount + projected return) over the Keyboard (numeric keypad).

### Parts

- Header - the typed amount, APR + duration line, and the resulting investment/payout amount.
- Keyboard - 0–9 + decimal + delete keys (reused Keyboard component).
- Alert / quick-amounts - contextual helpers (e.g. Wallet cap, +10K / +300K chips).

### Amount presets

The Value variant sets the typed amount and recomputes the return: 10K · 300K · 400K · 2M.

### Wallet mode

A separate mode for topping up / withdrawing within the investor’s remaining annual wallet cap - with a progress bar of the cap used and quick-amount chips.

### Result header

The header alone (QualifiedCalculator Header) - the projected-return display. Type Investment-cal vs wallet, with variants per amount / user tier.

### Code examples

```typescript
<QualifiedCalculator
  mode="invest"      // "invest" | "wallet"
  amount={10000}
  apr={0.14} termMonths={16}
  cap={qualifiedCap}
  onChange={setAmount}
/>
```

### Usage - Do and Don't

Do

Keep the result header pinned above the keypad so the projected return updates as they type.

Do

Use Wallet mode for top-up/withdraw, and show the remaining annual cap up front.

Don’t

Don’t show the result without an input - the header alone leaves the user no way to change the amount.

### Notes from the maintainer

> **Warning:** Previews are PNG exports: the nested REMOTE Headling component still uses IBM Plex Sans Arabic (won’t load here) → live instances are blocked. Re-font Headling to Noto Sans Arabic in its library to enable live docs.

> **Info:** QualifiedCalculator composes the reused Keyboard + Button + Alert + Label + ProgressBar + Headling - only the calculator shell + Header are bespoke.

> **Tip:** Qualified investors get higher amount caps + the Wallet mode; the invest mode mirrors InvestmentCalculator (08a) maths.

### Overview

Amount keypad v2 is where a qualified investor types the ticket. The amount, the rule and the CTA react to every key: valid amounts show the expected profit, invalid ones explain why and offer a fix.

### Anatomy

Amount hero on top, one context block under it (projection, ledger, presets or a fix), then the Keyboard and the Footer CTA.

Amount input · Valid

### States

One variant per situation. The CTA is enabled only when the amount can be invested or deposited.

Empty

Valid

Not multiple

Snap

Above cap

Above remaining

Wallet shortfall

Thousands

### Direction

LTR mirrors order and alignment and translates copy. Keyboard digits and numbers stay the same.

RTL

LTR

### Molecules

Built from the Hint atom and existing Syntropy components.

Amount hero

Title row

Summary card

Summary row

Presets

Quick action

### Atoms

Only one new atom; everything else is reused.

Hint · Muted

Hint · Warning

### Reused from Syntropy

- WalletChip · wallet label + balance in the title row.
- MoneyAmount · the typed amount (lg) and every value in the cards (sm).
- Tag · quick-amount pills.
- Button · secondary sm for snap suggestions and fix actions.
- Keyboard and Footer · the Product keypad and CTA, used as they are.

### Tokens

Semantic variables and text styles only.

- Colour · text/default, text/muted, text/warning (invalid amount, deposit needed), text/disabled (auto-completed zeros), text/success (profit delta), bg/surface, border/subtle.
- Radius · radius/md on cards. Spacing · space/xs to lg. Type · caption/12, body/13, body/14/semibold.

### Content rules

- Amounts go in multiples of 1,000, up to 500,000 per payment.
- Invalid amounts turn warning and the hint says why; offer the nearest fix as a button.
- CTA reads استثمر {amount} when valid, أودع {gap} وأكمل when the wallet is short, otherwise استثمر الآن disabled.
- Never write the word ريال; use the riyal icon.

### Accessibility

- Announce the hint whenever it changes tone.
- Warning colour is never the only signal: the hint text always explains.
- Fix buttons say the full amount they will set.

> **Tip:** Keep the CTA label in sync with the typed amount so screen-reader users hear what they are about to invest.

### Code examples

Flutter usage.

```dart
AmountKeypad(
  walletBalance: 112050,
  step: 1000,
  maxPerPayment: 500000,
  dealRemaining: 300000,
  onChanged: (amount) => ...,
  onInvest: (amount) => ...,
  textDirection: TextDirection.rtl,
)
```

### Usage · Do & Don’t

Do

Say why the amount is not accepted, right under it.

Don’t

Don’t only colour the amount. Colour alone does not explain the rule.

Do

Offer the nearest valid amounts as one-tap fixes.

Don’t

Don’t hide a wallet shortfall until checkout. Show the gap while typing.
